_comment: US names behind the industries on the Commodities board. Same shape as exposure_in.json: code is the ticker (the desk prices it through the US watch feed), industry must match a cost/revenue industry string in commodities.json, commodities lists the board ids the name attaches to. Every number traces to the document in intensity_source. Built commodity by commodity from 2026-09-09; a name may carry `sides` {commodity id: cost|revenue} to override the industry's side on one card (an integrated steel maker: coking coal cost, iron ore revenue).

names.label: Goodyear Tire & Rubber

names.pricing_power: Does not hedge commodity prices (10-K); offsets through central procurement, substitution and less material per tire. Sold the chemical business (synthetic rubber plants) on 31 October 2025 and now buys that too
names.note: Buys all its natural rubber on the world market (10-K).

names.label: Southern Copper
names.intensity: Copper 74.8% of net sales in 2025 (net sales a record $13,420.0 million; average LME copper $4.51/lb, COMEX $4.82/lb). Company sensitivity for 2026: a $0.10/lb change in the copper price changes estimated annual net income attributable to SCC by $120.0 million (a $1.00/lb molybdenum move $34.8 million, $0.10/lb zinc $25.6 million, $1.00/oz silver $14.1 million), assuming expected production and sales, unchanged 2025 tax rates and no cost changes. The Q2 2026 10-Q restates it for the remaining six months of 2026: $59.6 million per $0.10/lb copper ($18.0 million per $1.00/lb molybdenum, $13.3 million per $0.10/lb zinc, $7.1 million per $1.00/oz silver). 2025 operating cash cost $2.17/lb before by-product credits and $0.58/lb net of by-products; H1 2026 net cash cost was a credit of $(0.03)/lb on higher silver and molybdenum by-product revenue
names.intensity_source: Southern Copper Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001104659-26-021492, filed 2026-02-27), Item 7 'Metal Prices' sensitivity table and 'Copper' market discussion; Form 10-Q Q2 2026 (accession 0001104659-26-089169, filed 2026-07-31), Item 2 'Metal Prices'
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1: 'Prices for our products are principally a function of supply and demand and, with the exception of molybdenum, are established on COMEX and LME... From time to time, we have entered into hedging transactions to provide partial protection against future decreases in the market price of metals and we may do so under certain market conditions.' Item 7 Revenue Recognition: for certain copper and molybdenum sales, contracts allow pricing based on a month after shipment, 'in most cases within the following three months'; provisionally priced copper sales are marked to forward LME or COMEX prices each month until final settlement. 2025 net sales included $197.8 million of upward adjustments on provisionally priced sales
names.note: Sensitivity is stated on net income after tax, not EBITDA or revenue. Provisional pricing means part of a quarter's copper move settles through the next quarter's revenue. Revenues in US dollars; a significant part of costs is in Peruvian sol and Mexican pesos. Copper 74.8% of sales is the company's own figure; the remainder is molybdenum, silver, zinc and sulphuric acid by-products.

names.label: United Airlines
names.intensity: Aircraft fuel 21% of total operating expense in 2025: 4,663 million gallons consumed, fuel expense $11,396 million, average $2.44 a gallon including taxes (23% in 2024, 26% in 2023). Q2 2026 average price jumped to $4.19 a gallon (vs $2.34 a year earlier) and fuel expense rose $2.3 billion, or 84.1%, year on year
names.intensity_source: United Airlines Holdings Form 10-K for FY2025 (accession 0000100517-26-000023, filed 2026-02-12), Item 1 'Aircraft Fuel' table and Item 7A 'Aircraft Fuel'; Form 10-Q for Q2 2026 (accession 0000100517-26-000139, filed 2026-07-16), Item 2 operating statistics

Risk factors: 'If fuel prices were to then subsequently rise quickly, there may be a lag between the rise in fuel prices and any improvement of the revenue environment.'

names.label: ConocoPhillips
names.intensity: Pure upstream, 2,375 MBOED produced in 2025 (867 MMBOE), average realized $47.01 per BOE against $58.39 in 2024 (down 19%) on Brent $69.06 and WTI $64.81; crude realized $65.62/bbl, natural gas $4.44/Mcf (Lower 48 gas only $1.74/Mcf), NGL $21.07/bbl, bitumen $40.74/bbl. names.intensity_source: ConocoPhillips Form 10-K for fiscal 2025 (accession 0001163165-26-000009, filed 17 February 2026), Item 7 Business Environment (industry prices and average realized prices) and Results of Operations production and price tables; Item 7A Commodity Price Risk

names.label: Cameco
names.intensity: Uranium segment revenue C$2,874 million of consolidated revenue C$3,481.9 million in 2025, i.e. 82.5% (2,874 / 3,481.9); the rest is fuel services (conversion and fabrication), with the 49% Westinghouse stake equity-accounted. 2025 uranium average realized price US$65.53/lb (2024: US$58.45) against a UxC spot price of US$81.40/lb at 31 December 2025; 33.0 million lb delivered and 9.6 million lb purchased (including JV Inkai) in 2025. Company sensitivity for 2026: a US$5/lb rise in the uranium spot price adds C$36 million of revenue and C$8 million of adjusted net earnings but cuts cash flow by C$9 million (JV Inkai purchase entitlement of 4.4 million lb priced at a 5% discount to spot); a US$5/lb fall cuts revenue C$55 million, adjusted net earnings C$22 million and cash flow C$4 million. Expected realized price table at 31 December 2025 (US$/lb, spot scenarios $40/$60/$80/$100/$120/$140/$160): 2026 = 50/58/65/68/69/70/71; 2027 = 46/57/69/74/76/78/79; 2028 = 49/59/72/79/84/88/91; 2029 = 51/61/74/84 (higher scenarios continue). Long-term commitments of about 230 million lb after 2025 deliveries, averaging about 28 million lb a year over the next five years
names.intensity_source: Cameco 2025 annual MD&A dated 13 February 2026 (Exhibit 99.3 to Form 40-F, accession 0001193125-26-116229, filed 2026-03-19): 'Revenue, adjusted net earnings, and cash flow sensitivity analysis', 'Price sensitivity analysis: uranium segment', 2025 performance highlights and uranium segment results; Cameco 2025 consolidated financial statements (Exhibit 99.2 to the same 40-F), consolidated statement of earnings
names.lag: contract-lagged (company: 'changes to our average realized price will generally lag changes in market prices in both rising and falling price conditions'; delivery generally begins two years or more after signing; market-related prices are generally set a month or more before delivery)
names.pricing_power: MD&A 2025: 'We have a portfolio of long-term contracts, each bilaterally negotiated with customers, that have a mix of base-escalated pricing and market-related pricing mechanisms, including provisions that provide exposure to rising market prices while also protecting us when the market price is declining.' On the 2026 sensitivity: 'at the current price levels many of the market-related sales contracts we have delivered into or are delivering into this year are subject to ceiling prices and therefore are generally less sensitive than our purchase commitments.' Market-related contracts reference the spot or long-term price 'subject to specific terms unique to each contract, such as floors and ceilings set relative to market pricing at time of negotiation and typically escalated to time of delivery.' Fuel services is largely base-escalated. FX: US$1.01 billion of 2026 exposure hedged at 1.36 USDCAD
names.note: All money figures are Canadian dollars except uranium prices, which are US dollars. The 2026 upside is capped by ceiling prices in the contracts being delivered into; the lag given in the map is the company's own description. Cash flow moves against spot in the year of a JV Inkai purchase because the offsetting dividend arrives the following year. The 2029 realized-price row was cut off in the filing text extraction beyond the $100 scenario.

names.label: Archer-Daniels-Midland
names.intensity: ADM does not publish a per-unit crush-margin sensitivity. Its stated commodity exposure is the net commodity position (merchandisable inventories, purchase and sales contracts, energy and freight contracts, derivatives): for 2025 the weekly highest long position had a fair value of $541 million, lowest $(37) million, average $279 million, and a hypothetical 10% adverse price move on those positions is $54 million, $(4) million and $28 million respectively (2024 average $168 million / $17 million). Scale of the crush business: Crushing subsegment revenue $10,353 million of total revenue $80,269 million in 2025 (12.9%), Crushing operating profit $159 million in 2025 vs $844 million in 2024; Ag Services and Oilseeds segment operating profit $1,759 million. Cost of products sold $75,236 million on revenue $80,269 million (93.7%). In H1 2026 Crushing operating profit recovered to $284 million (vs $79 million), Q2 2026 alone $363 million (vs $33 million), including about $100 million of net positive mark-to-market and timing effects
names.intensity_source: ADM Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0000007084-26-000011, filed 2026-02-17), Item 7A Commodity Price Risk table and Note 17 subsegment revenue/operating profit; Form 10-Q Q2 2026 (accession 0000007084-26-000042, filed 2026-08-04), Item 2 segment results; Q2 2026 earnings release (8-K Exhibit 99.1, accession 0000007084-26-000040, 2026-08-04)
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 7A: 'The Company uses exchange-traded and OTC commodity instruments to manage its net position of merchandisable agricultural product inventories and forward cash purchase and sales contracts to reduce price risk caused by market fluctuations in agricultural commodities'; it also uses them 'as components of merchandising strategies designed to enhance margins'. Designated crush hedges (Note on derivatives, 10-K FY2025): futures and options hedge the purchase price of soybeans and the sale prices of soybean meal and oil 'proportionate to the soybean crushing process' at certain US crush plants; 'During the past 12 months, the Company hedged between 94% and 100% of the anticipated monthly soybean crush' at the designated facilities, with 0% to 100% of the next 12 months designated at 31 December 2025. Q2 2026 10-Q: past-12-month coverage 22% to 100%, 0% to 99% designated for the next 12 months. Corn: plants grind ~56 million bushels a month, 12% to 30% of monthly grind hedged in 2025. Q2 2026 release: crush margins 'supported by a constructive environment for biofuels, which was underpinned by the RVO, higher global energy prices'; the company 'expects to continue capitalizing on the constructive margin environment'
names.note: Earns the crush spread (meal plus oil value less bean cost) and merchandising margins, not the flat price; the 10% table measures the residual unhedged net position, not crush economics. Crushing is 12.9% of revenue but the Ag Services and Oilseeds segment as a whole is $61.6 billion of the $80.3 billion. Mark-to-market timing effects on hedges of committed capacity swing quarterly results (about +$100 million in Q2 2026, about -$200 million in H1 2026). No $/bushel crush sensitivity is stated in any document read.

names.label: Hershey
names.intensity: Cost of sales 66.5% of net sales in 2025 (cost of sales $7,769.9 million on net sales $11,692.6 million; gross margin 33.5% vs 47.3% in 2024). The 2025 cost-of-sales increase of $1,868.5 million included $736.6 million of higher commodity costs, $287.2 million of higher supply chain costs including tariffs, and $491.0 million of unfavourable mark-to-market on commodity derivatives hedging future years' purchases. Open commodity derivative notional $973.1 million at 31 December 2025 ($667.4 million at end-2024). Cocoa products are 'the most significant raw materials we use'; ICE cocoa futures averaged $3.65/lb in 2025 and $1.80/lb in H1 2026 (down about 51%). H1 2026 cost of sales $3,405.4 million included $142.4 million of favourable mark-to-market and lower commodity costs
names.intensity_source: Hershey Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001628280-26-008586, filed 2026-02-17), Item 7 Consolidated Results of Operations and Item 7A / Note 5 Commodity Price Risk; Form 10-Q Q2 2026 (accession 0001628280-26-050900, filed 2026-07-30), Item 2 and Item 3 Cocoa Products
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025: 'We attempt to minimize the effect of future raw material and energy price fluctuations by using derivatives and forward purchasing to cover future manufacturing requirements generally for 3 to 24 months... Our costs for major raw materials will not necessarily reflect market price fluctuations because of our forward purchasing and hedging practices.' 'Although we use forward contracts and commodity futures and options contracts to hedge commodity prices where possible, commodity price increases ultimately result in corresponding increases in our raw material and energy costs.' 2025 net sales carried about 6% price realization from higher list prices with about 1% volume loss from elasticity. Commodity derivatives are not hedge-accounted; mark-to-market runs through cost of sales and is excluded from segment income until the inventory is sold
names.note: Cocoa share of cost of sales is not disclosed; only the aggregate commodity cost increase is. The 3-to-24-month hedge book means 2025 P&L carried cocoa bought in the 2024 spike while H1 2026 spot fell 51%. Commodity notional is stated in thousands ($973,083) in the filing.

names.label: Weyerhaeuser
names.intensity: 2025 net sales $6,905 million; within Wood Products, structural lumber $2,037 million (29.5% of company net sales; $1,906 million in 2024), oriented strand board $762 million (11.0%; $979 million in 2024), engineered solid section $649 million. Net sales fell $219 million (3%) in 2025 'primarily due to a $264 million decrease in Wood Products net sales attributable to decreased sales realizations across most product lines', with Timberlands log sales down $18 million and Real Estate up $63 million. No $/MBF earnings sensitivity is stated; Item 7A covers long-term debt only
names.intensity_source: Weyerhaeuser Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001193125-26-051422, filed 2026-02-13), Item 7 'Consolidated Results' and 'Wood Products' segment net sales by product table; Item 1 'Five-Year Summary of Published Lumber Prices' and 'Published Oriented Strand Board Prices'; Item 7A
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1A: 'Competition from lumber imports could vary significantly and have a material effect on U.S. timber and lumber prices'; European imports 'have been more robust during strong domestic lumber market cycles, which can limit the benefits we realize from high timber and lumber prices.' Item 1A: 'We rely heavily on certain raw materials (principally wood fiber and chemicals) and energy sources (principally natural gas, electricity and fuel oil) in our manufacturing processes.' No lumber or OSB price hedging is described; realizations track published Random Lengths prices with the company's own log supply as the natural hedge
names.note: Timberlands (own fibre) and Real Estate are the rest of sales; log prices, not lumber, drive that segment. Lumber plus OSB is about 40% of company net sales, less of EBITDA in a weak year. The 10-K gives price tables, not a per-$10/MBF sensitivity.

names.label: D.R. Horton
names.intensity: Home sales cost of sales 77.7% of home sales revenue in fiscal 2025 (year ended 30 September 2025): $24,437.6 million on $31,432.0 million; home sales gross margin 21.5% vs 23.5% in fiscal 2024. Q3 fiscal 2026 (quarter to 30 June 2026): home sales cost of sales $6,809.6 million on home sales revenue $8,681.9 million (78.4%), gross margin 20.7% vs 21.8%; nine months $17,504.2 million on $22,240.1 million (78.7%). Lumber, steel and copper shares of home cost are not disclosed
names.intensity_source: D.R. Horton Form 10-K fiscal 2025 (accession 0000882184-25-000081, filed 2025-11-19), Item 7 Overview and segment revenue/cost tables; Form 10-Q Q3 fiscal 2026 (accession 0000882184-26-000096, filed 2026-07-23), Item 2 Overview and segment tables
names.pricing_power: 10-K fiscal 2025: 'We control construction costs by designing our homes efficiently, utilizing common house plans as consistently as possible and obtaining competitive bids for construction materials and labor'; 'we have contracts exceeding one year with certain suppliers of building materials that are cancelable at our option'. Risk factor: newly imposed tariffs on 'steel, aluminum and lumber, may raise our costs for these items'. Margin drivers stated are on the price side: fiscal 2025 'home sales gross margin decreased to 21.5% as we increased sales incentives, such as buydowns of mortgage rates'; Q3 fiscal 2026 margin 'reflecting the decline in our average sales price and higher sales incentives'; 'we currently expect sales incentives to remain elevated during the remainder of fiscal 2026 and into fiscal 2027'
names.note: Cost of sales for homes includes land, lot development and construction; no split between 'stick and brick' and land is given in the filings, so lumber share cannot be derived. The company's stated margin swings in fiscal 2025-2026 are attributed to incentives and price, not materials. Average closing price $370,400 in fiscal 2025, $362,000 in Q3 fiscal 2026.

names.label: Alcoa
names.intensity: Company statement for 2025: 'energy comprised approximately 24 percent of the Company's total alumina refining production costs and electric power comprised approximately 24 percent of the Company's primary aluminum production costs'; Alcoa generated about 11% of the power its smelters used in 2025 and bought the rest, generally under long-term arrangements. Revenue mix 2025: Aluminum segment third-party sales $8,359 million (third-party aluminum $8,515 million less $156 million of energy sales and hedge results) and Alumina segment third-party sales $4,447 million (alumina $3,710 million plus bauxite $737 million) against consolidated sales of $12,831 million, so the Aluminum segment is about 65% of sales (8,359 / 12,831) and Alumina about 35%. No dollars-per-tonne LME or alumina price sensitivity is stated in the 10-K; Item 7A refers only to Note P (derivatives). Q2 2026: adjusted EBITDA $901 million, up $306 million sequentially 'primarily due to higher aluminum prices and shipments', partly offset by 'higher energy prices, primarily fuel oil and diesel increases associated with the Middle East conflict' and Section 232 tariff costs on Canadian metal
names.intensity_source: Alcoa Form 10-K FY2025 (accession 0001193125-26-077167, filed 2026-02-26), Item 1 'Energy Facilities and Sources' and 'Aluminum' pricing discussion, Item 7 segment tables (Alumina and Aluminum third-party sales) and Note E 'Sales'; Alcoa Q2 2026 results press release dated 16 July 2026 (Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K, accession 0001193125-26-306118)
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1A: the price of primary aluminum is 'the underlying base metal component, which is typically based on quoted prices from the LME; (ii) the regional premium... associated with the physical delivery of metal to a particular region' plus a product premium; alumina is sold under contracts with 'the API price basis and a negotiated adjustment basis'. Energy: 'Pricing may be fixed, indexed to an underlying fuel source or other index such as LME, cost-based, or based on regional market pricing.' Note P: several power contracts are embedded derivatives that index the price of power to the LME price of aluminum (one also to the Midwest premium), so 'Increase in LME price and/or the Midwest premium results in a higher cost of power'. Q2 2026 release: Aluminum third-party revenue rose 31% sequentially 'partially offset by impacts from certain energy contracts linked to metal pricing'
names.note: Both figures are the company's own cost-share statements, not a per-$100/t sensitivity; Alcoa publishes per-tonne sensitivities only in its earnings slide decks, which were not in the filings opened. LME-linked power contracts (Brazil, Norway, Quebec) claw back part of an aluminum price rise through power cost. Natural gas exposure is concentrated in the Western Australia and Spain refineries; the 10-K gives no gas share separate from the 24% energy share of refining cost.

names.label: International Paper
names.industry: Integrated paper makers with own pulp
names.pricing_power: 10-K FY2025 Item 1A: 'We rely heavily on the use of certain raw materials (principally virgin wood fiber, recycled fiber, caustic soda, starch and adhesives), energy sources (principally biomass, natural gas, electricity and fuel oil) and third-party transport companies... we have not always been able to, and may in the future be unable to, recoup past or future increases in the costs of any raw materials, energy sources or transportation sources from customers... where we are able to recoup our cost increases, there may be a delay between the onset of the cost increases and the recoupment.' We have employed and expect to continue to employ, strategies, including hedging a portion of our energy costs.' Q4 2025 MD&A: EMEA 'input costs are expected to be higher primarily driven by elevated energy costs' in Q1 2026
names.note: The 10-K and Q2 2026 10-Q name fibre (virgin wood fibre, recycled fibre/OCC) and energy (biomass, natural gas, electricity, fuel oil) as the principal inputs but give no percentage of cost of goods sold for either, and no $/t sensitivity; the only number is the 10% adverse-move test on the energy hedge book. Sales contracts to date 'specify the quantity to be delivered, the price, payment terms and the period of delivery' for purchased U3O8 held at conversion facilities

names.label: Caterpillar

names.label: Solaris Energy Infrastructure
